Question 4

Find the first four non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of the function f(x)=1+x.

a
1+x=x+3x22−5x38+7x448+⋯
b
1+x=1−x4+x216−3x396+⋯
c
1+x=1+x2−x28+x348+⋯
d
1+x=x+x22−x38+x416+⋯
e
1+x=1+x2−x28+x316+⋯
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The Maclaurin expansion of f(x) is f(x)=f(0)+f′(0)x+f″(0)2!x2+f‴(0)3!x3+⋯.

Computing the necessary derivatives, we get f(x)=1+x=(1+x)1/2f(0)=(1+0)1/2=1,f′(x)=(12)(1+x)−1/2f′(0)=12(1+0)−1/2=12,f″(x)=(−12)⋅(12)(1+x)−3/2=−14(1+x)−3/2f″(0)=−14(1+0)−3/2=−14,f‴(x)=(−32)⋅(−14)(1+x)−5/2=38(1+x)−5/2f‴(0)=38(1+0)−5/2=38.

Therefore, the Maclaurin expansion is

1+x=(1)+(12)x+(−14)x22!+(38)x33!+⋯=1+x2−x28+x316+⋯.
